1. Santa Monica: A Plan for Our Future - City Restructuring and Associated Modifications to the Fiscal Year 2020-21 Budget Resulting from Economic Impacts of COVID-19 Pandemic SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT - See attachments G and H.
Recommended Actions
1) Staff recommends that Council authorize the following budget actions:
(a)               Authorize staff to drawdown and use the entire $9.7 million Economic Uncertainty Reserve to mitigate short-term losses in FY 2019-2020;
(b)               Authorize staff t o release $9.2 million from assigned reserves in the General Fund and use those funds to mitigate short-term losses in FY 2019-20;
( c)               Authorize staff to lower the General Fund Contingency Reserve formula from 15% to 12.5% in FY 2020-2021;
(d)               Authorize staff to establish a $20 million Shutdown Reserve for FY 2020-2021;
(e)               Authorize staff to return $24 million of the Boeing/Gillette settlement funds from the Water Fund to the General Fund in FY 2019-2020;
(f)               Authorize staff to have the General Fund r e tain one quarter of the FY 2020-2021 Measure GSH transaction and use tax revenue;
(g)               Authorize staff to: ( i ) suspend the currently scheduled FY 2020-2021 $7.3 million pension fund paydown payment, (ii) shift from a 13-year to 15-year schedule for the pe n sion fund paydown, and (iii) suspend the FY 2020-2021 and FY 2021-2022 pension fund paydown payments under the new 15-year paydown schedule;
(h)               Authorize staff to establish a $1 million Economic Recovery Fund in FY 2020-2021 ; and,
(i) Appropriate FY 2019- 20 CIP expenditure adjustments to alternative resources as set forth in Attachment A .
2) Staff also recommends that Council authorize the following personnel actions:
a)               Authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department and classification i n Attachment A , wi th the exception of positions whose duties relate directly and substantially to the Santa Monica Pier; authorize staff to issue layoff notices to employees occupying those positions as necessary to accomplish the restructuring plan in Att achment A and in accordance with applicable provisions of the City’s Charter and Municipal Code; and authorize staff to enter into negotiations with the labor groups representing the laid off employees over the impacts of the layoffs; and
b)               Authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department and classification in Attachment A whose duties relate directly and substantially to the Santa Monica Pier; authorize staff to issue layoff notices to employees occupying those positions as necessary to accomplish the re structuring plan in Attachment A and in accordance with applicable provisions of the City’s Charter and Municipal Code ; and authorize staff to enter into negotiations with the labor groups representing the laid off employees over the impac ts of the layoffs .
3)               Staff also recommends that Coun c il p rovide staff with direction regarding principles and priorities for allocating $2 million in ongoing funds beginning in FY 2020-21 , and other remaining available funds , if any, for restoring progr ams should the City’s circumstances post-COVID-19 permit such restoration.

(NOT APPROVED)

  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  MAY 5, 2020

A special meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor McKeown at 3:00 p.m., on
Tuesday, May 5, 2020, via teleconference pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 at
https://primetime.bluejeans.com/a2m/live-event/xzurkqeh.

Roll Call:  Present:  Mayor Kevin McKeown
  Mayor Pro Tem Terry O’Day
  Councilmember Gleam Davis
  Councilmember Sue Himmelrich
  Councilmember Ana M. Jara
  Councilmember Greg Morena
  Councilmember Ted Winterer

  Also Present:  Interim City Manager Lane Dilg
  Interim City Attorney George Cardona
  City Clerk Denise Anderson-Warren

CONVENE  On order of the Mayor, the City Council convened at 3:00 p.m., with all
  members present.

STAFF  8.A. Santa Monica: A Plan for Our Future - City Restructuring and
ADMINISTRATIVE  Associated Modifications to the Fiscal Year 2020-21 Budget Resulting
ITEMS:  from Economic Impacts of COVID-19 Pandemic, was presented.
CITY RESTRUCTURING
  Recommended Actions
  1) Staff recommends that Council authorize the following budget actions:
  (a) Authorize staff to drawdown and use the entire $9.7 million
  Economic Uncertainty Reserve to mitigate short-term losses in FY
  2019-2020;
  (b) Authorize staff to release $9.2 million from assigned reserves in
  the General Fund and use those funds to mitigate short-term losses
  in FY 2019-20;
  (c) Authorize staff to lower the General Fund Contingency Reserve
  formula from 15% to 12.5% in FY 2020-2021;
  (d) Authorize staff to establish a $20 million Shutdown Reserve for
  FY 2020- 2021;
  (e) Authorize staff to return $24 million of the Boeing/Gillette
  settlement funds from the Water Fund to the General Fund in FY
  2019-2020;

  1  May 5, 2020
   (f) Authorize staff to have the General Fund retain one quarter of the
  FY 2020-2021 Measure GSH transaction and use tax revenue;
  (g) Authorize staff to: (i) suspend the currently scheduled FY 2020-
  2021 $7.3 million pension fund paydown payment, (ii) shift from a
  13-year to 15-year schedule for the pension fund paydown, and
  (iii) suspend the FY 2020- 2021 and FY 2021-2022 pension fund
  paydown payments under the new 15-year paydown schedule;
  (h) Authorize staff to establish a $1 million Economic Recovery Fund
  in FY 2020-2021; and,
  (i) Appropriate FY 2019-20 CIP expenditure adjustments to
  alternative resources as set forth in Attachment A.
2) Staff also recommends that Council authorize the following personnel
  actions:
  a) Authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department
  and classification in Attachment A, with the exception of positions
  whose duties relate directly and substantially to the Santa Monica
  Pier; authorize staff to issue layoff notices to employees occupying
  those positions as necessary to accomplish the restructuring plan in
  Attachment A and in accordance with applicable provisions of the
  City’s Charter and Municipal Code; and authorize staff to enter
  into negotiations with the labor groups representing the laid off
  employees over the impacts of the layoffs; and
  b) Authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department
  and classification in Attachment A whose duties relate directly and
  substantially to the Santa Monica Pier; authorize staff to issue
  layoff notices to employees occupying those positions as necessary
  to accomplish the restructuring plan in Attachment A and in
  accordance with applicable provisions of the City’s Charter and
  Municipal Code; and authorize staff to enter into negotiations with
  the labor groups representing the laid off employees over the
  impacts of the layoffs.
3) Staff also recommends that Council provide staff with direction
  regarding principles and priorities for allocating $2 million in ongoing
  funds beginning in FY 2020-21, and other remaining available funds, if
  any, for restoring programs should the City’s circumstances post-
  COVID-19 permit such restoration.

Dr. Ben Drati spoke on behalf of the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School
District.

Members of the public David Fairbank, Mr. Cowar, Jennifer Cowan,
Benjamin Steers, Stacy Weakenpaine, Therese Kelly, Chris Pico, Lauralee
Ashe, Michael Tarbet, Michael Goldstrum, Noah Sodi, Jason Ritterben,
Cris Gutierrez, Jon Kean, Wesley Swung, Joanne Berlin, Jenny Amaya,
Sharon Kingsley, Zina Josephs, Allison Hovel, Rachel Weinstein, Tricia
Crane, Lorraine Fuentes, Sonya Sultan, Puja Thomas-Patel, Marcy Kaplan,

  2  May 5, 2020
 Connor Everetts, Matt Stauffer, Gail Gutierrez, Carlos Rubio, Calisse
Lindsey, Hillsbran Mercedes, Patti Braun, Michael Hanush, Cynthia
Rhodes, Jayro Queme, Dr. Ashley Silvera, Jennifer Wolf, Michael Soloff,
Noah Garrison, Rene Buchannan, Denise McGranahan, Ellis Raskin, Angel
Towler, Noel Lewis, Tara Barauskas, Sheri Batalla, Phil Brock, Nico
Bardicki, Carl Hansen, Carol Lemlein, Jason Kligier, Barbi Applequist,
Ann Dudek, Angela Scott, Shawn Landres, Janet Gollery McKeithen, Nina
Fresco, Tina Grossman, Denny Zane, Ericka Lesley, Shari Davis, Jennifer
Kennedy, Marianne LaGuardia, Suzy Borlido, Joe Schmidt and Benjamin
Kay spoke on the recommended action.

Questions asked and answered of staff included: there are questions and
concerns from the school district as to whether or not the cuts being
proposed for field access is a breach of contract with the school district;
isn’t this a first step, and are there other opportunities to make budget
decisions; how will the voluntary separation program adjust the layoffs
being proposed; if someone in the city is laid off, they have a year to be
reinstated in their job, could the Council choose to extend the reinstatement
period by an additional year; how would the city be able to request
volunteers to cover staffing for school district field access instead of
providing Community and Cultural Services (CCS) staff; how do we
balance the cost against the fees that we charge for services; how many
members are in the Preserving Our Diversity (POD) program; are we
actually going to eliminate 300 positions, even with the number of
employees who took advantage of the voluntary separation plan; the people
who are laid off, are they able to get unemployment; what is the total
number of layoff notices that will be issued, or is there a range; in so much
as Council accepts cuts in classifications, can unions negotiate those
classifications; how are the negotiations with labor negotiators going to be
conveyed to council, in open or closed session; with those who will
ultimately be laid off, will they receive services from the city to help them
transition to other employment; can you explain why other options have not
been considered prior to proposing layoffs, and, why were negotiations
with labor groups not included before now; what role will the bargaining
unions have to be involved in the final layoff plans; how is the Fire Chief
going to deal with the bargaining union in order to bring about the
suggested staffing changes; is there any way to save a specific position
without going into the $2 million dedicated to restoration; are there any
specific programs that the city would want to have restored using the $2
million; does it take more of Finance staff team if the Council decided to go
to a quarterly budget process; if we’re going to promote cleanliness, is that
possible with the reduction of painters; can the revisioning project be
completed with the impact of COVID-19 and a reduction in staff; for Fire,
is 35 staff members the minimum daily number of Firefighters needed;
does Fire currently have staffing that is being proposed as part of their
budget cut; will Council have options when this plan comes back after

  3  May 5, 2020
   labor negotiations; was the process to remove certain programs first and
  then eliminate positions associated to those programs; is there capacity to
  make deeper cuts in the Office of Communications; what is the cost for the
  Print Shop; is there any Emergency Operation Center (EOC) work that is
  being done that certain staff cost could be recovered from the federal
  government; and do cross-trained individuals who have disaster services
  training get any special status, or do we get a stronger claim from the
  federal government for those workers.

  Councilmember Morena recused himself from this vote in order to avoid
Councilmember Morena  any perceived conflict of interest because his family owns a restaurant on
excused at 8:17 p.m.  the Pier.

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember Jara, to
  authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department and
  classification in Attachment A whose duties relate directly and substantially
  to the Santa Monica Pier; authorize staff to issue layoff notices to
  employees occupying those positions as necessary to accomplish the
  restructuring plan in Attachment A and in accordance with applicable
  provisions of the City’s Charter and Municipal Code; and authorize staff to
  enter into negotiations with the labor groups representing the laid off
  employees over the impacts of the layoffs.
Councilmember Morena
returned at 8:19 p.m.  The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Himmelrich, Davis, Winterer, Jara,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Morena

  Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember
  Himmelrich, to approve and authorize all items 1(a) through 1(i) of the
  recommended action. The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Jara, Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to:
  whether or not to consider Architectural Review Board (ARB) design
  review options; concerns about asking for decisions about proposed
  staffing cuts without having analysis to show who these cuts impact; and,
  explanations for eliminating some positions, but creating others instead.

  Motion by Councilmember Morena, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem O’Day,

  4  May 5, 2020
 to authorize the abolition of the positions identified by Department and
classification in Attachment A, with the exception of positions whose
duties relate directly and substantially to the Santa Monica Pier; authorize
staff to issue layoff notices to employees occupying those positions as
necessary to accomplish the restructuring plan in Attachment A and in
accordance with applicable provisions of the City’s Charter and Municipal
Code; and authorize staff to enter into negotiations with the labor groups
representing the laid off employees over the impacts of the layoffs.

The motion was approved by the following vote:

AYES:  Councilmembers Winterer, Davis, Himmelrich, Morena,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
NOES:  Councilmember Jara
ABSENT: None

Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to:
Collaboration and Communication with the community as a whole; guided
by the message of Social Justice, how do we protect and preserve those
vulnerable, Health and Safety programs, with better cost recovery; and
Resiliency is key where value to spending resources on Mobility and
Sustainability.

Motion by Councilmember Davis, seconded by Councilmember Jara, to
divide the money into five buckets in the amount of $400,000 each:
1) increasing the POD program; 2) Youth Programs; 3) Outdoor health; 4)
Mobility; and 5) Sustainability.

Friendly amendment Councilmember Winterer, to move the dollar amounts
around, with a maximum of $400,000, but relatively equal. Considered
friendly by the maker and seconder.

Friendly amendment Councilmember Winterer, to use funds from the
Housing Trust Fund to increase the POD program and potentially refund
LAFLA. This was considered direction with no addition to the motion.

Friendly amendment by Councilmember Winterer, to find an expenditure
neutral way to preserve design review of large projects and continue to
provide the ARB’s pro bono services to the Planning Commission. The
motion was considered friendly by the maker and seconder of the motion.

Friendly amendment by Councilmember Himmelrich proposed priorities 1)
feeding people; 2) keeping people in their homes, including the POD
program and then 3) restoring Youth programs. The motion was not
considered friendly by the maker.

  5  May 5, 2020
   Substitute motion by Councilmember Morena to: 1) set aside $110,000 to
  preserve the agreement with SMMUSD; 2) focus on principles and
  analysis: look at cuts through a social justice lens, labor negotiations: 3)
  review of revenue and expenditures per fund; 4) preserving revenue
  generation processes across departments; 5) re-envision the grants
  programs; 6) Cleanliness in the City, and look at ways to preserve the best
  of the city. The motion failed due to a lack of a second.

  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day supported the motion.

  Friendly amendment by Mayor McKeown, to make the buckets to be more
  flexible and put more emphasis on the people in need, then distribute the
  remainder of the money for other priorities, including The Westside Food
  Bank and Meals on Wheels. The motion was considered friendly by the
  maker and seconder.

  Councilmember Morena proposed a friendly amendment to earmark the
  $110,000 for SMMUSD, grant programs for afterschool programs, and
  consideration for revenue generating programs. The motion was considered
  friendly by the maker and seconder.

  The motion for direction, with amendments was approved by the following
  vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Morena, Himmelrich, Davis, Winterer, Jara,
  Mayor Pro Tem O’Day, Mayor McKeown
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the City Council meeting adjourned at 10:46 p.m.
  in memory of the nine Santa Monica residents who have died from the
  coronavirus.

  ATTEST:  APPROVED:

  Denise Anderson-Warren  Kevin McKeown
  City Clerk  Mayor

  6  May 5, 2020
